cards.text: Paul's writing to the church in Philippi, and he's in chains while he does it (Philippians 1:13). Timothy is right there with him, in on this letter (Philippians 1:1). Now Paul says he hopes in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to them soon.

cards.question: Paul hopes to send Timothy to Philippi soon. What does Paul say he hopes that visit does for him?

answers.text: He'll be cheered to learn how they're doing
He'll get help preparing for his trial
He'll get supplies for his time in chains

cards.text: Then Paul says he has nobody else like Timothy. NOBODY, friend, and I'd want THAT carved on my handle right under my name.

cards.question: Paul says Timothy will genuinely ___ for the Philippians' needs.
Besides Timothy, Paul says, all the others look after the interests of Jesus Christ, not their own.

cards.text: Paul says all the others look after "their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ." Those two words, "own interests," showed up a few lines back too, when Paul told the church to look to the interests of others as well (Philippians 2:4).

cards.question: The Philippians already know Timothy's proven worth. How does Paul say Timothy has served with him?

answers.text: Like a child with his father
Like a soldier with his captain
Like a servant with his master

cards.text: Timothy has served with Paul like a child with his father, to advance the gospel. My six cookie cutter kids used to call me Papa, so friend, this one gets me RIGHT in the apron.
So Timothy's the man for the job. But Paul isn't sending him off just yet.

cards.question: Paul is waiting before he sends Timothy to Philippi. When does he hope to send him?

answers.text: As soon as he sees what happens with him
As soon as the Philippians write him back
As soon as he finishes writing this letter

cards.question: Even in chains, Paul trusts in the Lord that he himself will come to the Philippians soon.

cards.text: Look at this man. He's in CHAINS, and he's out here making travel plans, while I spent years in a junk drawer and never once planned a trip past the rubber bands.
But there's someone else Paul thought it necessary to send back to Philippi: Epaphroditus. Paul calls him his brother, fellow worker and fellow soldier, and he's the Philippians' own messenger.

cards.question: Paul says Epaphroditus, the Philippians' messenger, is also a minister to Paul's needs.
Epaphroditus has been longing for all of them back in Philippi. But something has him distressed. What is it?

answers.text: The Philippians heard he was ill

cards.text: The man's the one who got sick, and HE'S the one distressed because THEY heard about it? I bet he's the friend texting the group chat "I'm FINE" from the hospital bed.
And friend, this was no small thing. Epaphroditus was sick indeed, nearly unto death.

cards.question: Paul says God had mercy on Epaphroditus, and on no one else.

cards.text: God had mercy on Paul too, Paul says, to spare him sorrow upon sorrow. I think losing a friend like Epaphroditus would have hit Paul hard.

cards.question: Paul is all the more eager to send Epaphroditus home. He says that when the Philippians see him again they may rejoice, and Paul may be less ___.
Paul tells the Philippians to welcome Epaphroditus in the Lord with great joy and to honor men like him. What does Paul say Epaphroditus nearly died for?

cards.text: Epaphroditus did it, Paul says, "risking his life to make up for your deficit of service to me." Friend, a man like that gets the first cookie out of EVERY batch in my bakery.
